promptPrefix:
Use case: style-transfer. Edit the supplied FIRST Rocky style sample into ONE NEW male gym-character sprite. Input image is STYLE ONLY: keep its moderate coarse pixel-art density, square staircase edges, mature face, adult proportions, restrained material shades and dark outlines. Replace the person completely with the requested character. Do NOT copy Rocky's gray suit, towel, shoes or boxing pose onto other characters. Do NOT simplify into the rejected very coarse version, and do NOT create a polished high-detail comic illustration. Obvious substantial square pixels, about 3 flat shade clusters per material, no realistic skin texture, individual hair strands, fine stubble, gradients or antialiasing.
PRODUCTION FRAME: square transparent canvas, ONE centered complete full-body adult man, three-quarter front view, consistent lighting from upper left. Same head scale and human body height across the full series: body about 76 percent of canvas height, head about 11 percent, feet baseline around 89 percent. Leave generous empty transparent margins on ALL sides, minimum 8 percent including below feet and above hair/props. No clipped extremities. Props must remain compact and must not make the body smaller. No floor, background, furniture, card, frame, text, numbers, halo, aura, shadow or watermark. Genuinely transparent exterior, opaque character interior.
PHYSICAL POWER is character anatomy, not zoom or bag size. Follow the stated power band: early men are ordinary and not muscular; later athletes have developed chest/shoulders/arms/legs; final heroes are extremely powerful. Keep all mature, no chibi or oversized childish head. Only one clearly recognizable character and one main gym joke.
powerEnglish: Band0/8: ordinary healthy untrained man. Narrow/modest shoulders, thin normal upper arms, no visible pec or six-pack definition, not a champion body; not sickly or humiliating. Relaxed everyday posture.
Band1/8: ordinary lightly active adult with modest tone, not an action hero or bodybuilder. Still slim/moderate shoulders and small arms, a little more composed than a beginner.
Band2/8: fit light athletic adult, moderate shoulder and forearm development, firm legs, no large hypertrophy. Clearly less massive than serious fighters.

Band3/8: well-trained human athlete. Developed rounded shoulders, muscular chest and upper arms, dense forearms, strong thighs; visibly more powerful than an ordinary beginner at the SAME body height.
Band4/8: strong trained fighter. Dense shoulders, forearms and thighs, confident stable stance. Lean heroes retain identity but visibly athletic physique, not fragile civilian anatomy.
Band5/8: powerful large strength athlete, broad chest, heavy shoulders, large arms and strong legs. Visibly greater muscular bulk than lower bands without zooming.
Band6/8: heroic muscular anatomy, broad dense torso and strong limbs. Recognizable character and mature face; strength evident even without magic, weapons or background.
Band7/8: superhuman or cybernetic heavy athletic silhouette, very developed chest/shoulder girdle, substantial forearms and powerful planted legs. Gear never hides a tiny body.

Band8/8: legendary physical power, most imposing adult silhouettes. Huge strong chest, shoulders and limbs, planted stance. Lean iconic heroes still clearly powerful and athletic. Atlas80 must be the mightiest silhouette of the whole series, not a small man behind a huge globe.
